record.file_problem: GitHub repository metadata, README, and file list only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports a baseline application of the refusal-direction projection ablation and refusal outcomes on a new model. The defense itself is a scale-down, not a reproduction of the full LAT method.
record.gate_note: The README reports eight evaluation conditions, including the base-model ablation result. The direction-cosine and norm measurements describe changes after defense training but do not test whether the direction mediates refusal, so they are not rows. Training-loss values likewise do not directly measure a claim version. Results for the trained defense are recorded as findings, not evidence that an untrained model naturally has the reported behavior.
record.test_reason: Reproduces difference-in-means refusal-direction ablation on Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct: harmful-prompt refusal drops from 1.00 to 0.00 (rows A–B). It also trains a LoRA against this ablation and measures robustness and harmless-prompt refusal, which bears on V3's 'training against ablation adds robustness' part.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors call it an 'honest null': 100% robustness to static and adaptive ablation achieved only through a constant refusal policy on harmless prompts too. They attribute it to the stripped-down recipe, not targeted LAT in general.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the refusal-direction projection ablation associated with #41, but evaluates it at L=14 in the reported matrix. The defense is a scale-down reproduction of targeted LAT with a small LoRA and refusal-only data, omitting the mixed harmless-answer and capability data and utility term described for the published method. Repository type: tool/experiment; README describes it as a scale-down reproduction.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome depends on whether the evaluated model is the base model or the LAT-LoRA-defended model; the defended model refuses harmless prompts as well as harmful prompts. The README also reports one seed, one LoRA configuration, and one attack layer.

fits_no_version.finding: After defense training the refit refusal direction has cosine 0.804 with r_base at L=14 (0.431–0.875 across layers), with norm down 16%. The authors attribute this to a degenerate policy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training against direction ablation shifts the difference-in-means direction, but under collapse the direction becomes ill-defined.

record.problems: The README notes one seed, one LoRA configuration, one attack layer, and a harmless evaluation set of 10 prompts. It describes a scale-down that omits parts of the published LAT recipe, so the null result is not evidence about the full method. No uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: None of the separately reported A–H evaluation conditions were left out. Direction cosine/norm and training-loss values were omitted because they do not directly measure a claim version's refusal behavior.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal; general-capability preservation after ablation on the base model; only 10 prompts, one layer choice.
Whether existing jailbreaks (e.g., GCG) work by suppressing the direction; full LAT recipe with harmless/capability data and utility term.

missing.what: Direction cosine and norm between base and defended models
missing.locator: README, 'Did the defense move the refusal direction?' table

record.verdict_notes: This is a GitHub README only; numbers are on 10 prompts, one seed, one layer, no uncertainty. The V1 reproduction relies on code imported from repo #41. The reader marked V3 untested, but the study directly measures robustness of training against ablation. That robustness is the V3 claim's own intervention, so rows C–H are linked to V3.

versions.untested_parts: Tests harmful-prompt refusal after ablation at L=14 on the base model. It does not test adding the direction, ablation at every layer and position as a complete intervention, or whether ablating it preserves general capability.
No weight-edit or abliteration removal is tested.

The defense is trained with ablation hooks, but the reported defense behavior is deliberately induced by training; the README reports method performance rather than behavior arising without that inducement.
No test of affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No cross-language, model-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer test.
The README reports one defense-training recipe, not a comparison of training methods or stages that tests when a removable direction forms.
